title: Scheduled network proxy concierge onramp for air-gapped/VPC upgrade requests
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers in highly restricted environments (air-gapped, strict VPC egress policies, corporate proxies on heavy inspection) repeatedly request staged upgrades and network remediation assistance. Current intake funnels these to engineering tickets or ad-hoc support, creating long lead times and inconsistent outcomes. Goal: introduce a prescriptive, low-effort "concierge onramp" pattern that combines an automated intake rubric, a temporary scheduled reverse-proxy option, and a clear staged upgrade checklist. This ticket defines the PM scope: acceptance criteria, rollout gating, handoffs to Solutions Eng, and UX surface in the intake form to reduce triage time and increase first-contact resolution for networking/upgrade constraints.
acceptance_criteria: Public intake form updated to capture egress rules, allowed IPs, OS/hypervisor and upgrade window preferences
Automated rubric assigns priority buckets and recommended remediation (proxy+whitelist/patch vs. local operator playbook) within 6 hours
Concierge scheduled-proxy option implemented as an Ops-run play with an internal runbook and 2-hour booking slots for verified enterprise customers
Solutions Eng runbook includes rollback scripts, offline artifact packaging steps, and a standardized post-upgrade validation checklist
Measure: reduce average triage-to-resolution for network/upgrade requests from 21 days to <= 7 days for high-priority customers within first quarter after launch
decisions: We will offer a temporary scheduled reverse-proxy (customer-approved) rather than requiring permanent network changes
Concierge will be scoped as a paid add-on for non-SMB accounts; initial pilot will be free for 3 strategic customers to validate the workflow
Security review required prior to first scheduled proxy usage; use customer-signed authorization template
Default routing in the intake rubric will prefer native fixes (whitelist, local package) over proxy if customer's network policies allow it
